source.filename: YOUTH ECO SUMMIT TOPICS AND GUIDELINES-2027.pdf
source.theme: Waste segregation, the need of the hour
source.dates: Student registrations and competition submissions run from 1 October to 5 November 2026. The deadline is 5 November 2026, 11:59 p.m. IST. School and teacher registration remain available after this deadline.
generalRules: Submit original work that reflects your own ideas and voice.
Cite sources for any content you use or are inspired by. Verify facts and statistics.
AI may be used for research or reference. AI-generated content in a submission receives a 15-point deduction. Credit any sources used or inspiring the work.
Use underscores instead of spaces or special characters in the submission title. Include your school, class, category, project title and author names.

clarificationItems.detail: The PDF did not supply dates. The user confirmed student registrations and competition submissions are open and close on 5 November. This cutoff does not apply to school or teacher registration. The website uses the confirmed 1 October 2026 launch as opening, with the deadline interpreted as the end of 5 November 2026 in India Standard Time; 6 November 00:00 IST is the exclusive closing boundary.

The original PDF overview lists Classes 7–10 for Waste to Art and its craft section lists Classes 9–12. On 6 October 2026 the user confirmed all four class bands: 5–6, 7–8, 9–10 and 11–12. Website eligibility is Classes 5–12; the original PDF remains unchanged.
The four art criteria total 90 marks. No additional 10 marks are supplied; do not normalise to 100 without confirmation.

On 6 October 2026 the user confirmed a 15-point deduction for AI-generated submission content across all competitions. AI research and reference remain permitted with credited sources. This user decision supersedes the original PDF’s conflicting disqualification statements; the original PDF is retained unchanged.
The eco-business slide template is referenced but was not included with the PDF. Do not invent its headings.

competitions.title: Open Letter
competitions.description: Write directly to your school, community or local leader about the choices that shape a cleaner future.

topics.title: Waste Segregation: The Future Is Still in Our Hands
topics.prompt: Write an open letter explaining why separating wet, dry and harmful waste matters. Show how mixing waste creates landfills, while segregation allows recycling and composting. Connect small kitchen and classroom habits to a cleaner future.

references.title: Example open letter for climate justice

notes: Typed work only; handwritten entries are not accepted.
Use a title, introduction, body, conclusion and references. Include the author byline.
No images, movie clips or hyperlinks in the piece; hyperlinks are allowed only in references.
Keep the work personal and original, build ideas logically, use verified facts and offer a solution or call to action.
Optional infographics may accompany the open letter.
rewards: The top two pieces in each written category are intended for publication and promotion in leading digital news dailies and other publications.
Other winning work may be featured on partner portals, including YuWaah and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. Publication is subject to partner arrangements.

criteria.title: Personal opinion, suggestions and innovative ideas
Relevant examples, statistics and accurate research

notes: AI-generated submission content receives a 15-point deduction, as confirmed on 6 October 2026. AI research or reference is permitted; sources must be credited.

competitions.title: Article
competitions.description: Build a grounded argument about sustainable technology or the next chapter of cleanliness.

topics.title: Technology and Responsibility
topics.prompt: Explore the hidden environmental costs of devices and online life. Consider e-waste, manufacturing, data centres and personal habits, and imagine technology designed for repair, upgrades, reuse and recycling.

topics.title: Swachh Bharat 2.0: Can Cleanliness Campaigns Transform Waste?

competitions.description: Look closely at a real family decision or the possibility of a community built around repair and sharing.

topics.title: Keep, Repair, or Throw Away: A Family Reflection

topics.title: A Community Built on Repair, Reuse, and Sharing

competitions.title: Short Film
competitions.description: Use documentary, animation or fiction to make an environmental story worth watching.

topics.title: Voices from the Bin
topics.prompt: Give waste from your neighbourhood a voice and personality. Use humour, drama, animation or mockumentary to reveal something surprising about daily habits.

topics.title: The Day the Waste Vanished
topics.prompt: Every scrap of waste disappears overnight. Film the ripple effects to explore how deeply waste is embedded in our routines.

topics.title: The Day My Bin Refused to Work
topics.prompt: A household bin refuses more waste until a family changes its habits. Build a serious or comic narrative around the bin’s strike and the choices people make without thinking.

topics.title: One Technology and One Climate Problem
topics.prompt: Choose a technology and a climate challenge—such as AI and energy, smartphones and e-waste, or renewable technology and changing weather—and explore their connection through a character or moment.

notes: Maximum five minutes, MP4, 120 MB and 1080p. Landscape or portrait is accepted.
Build a compelling narrative, a clear message and a call to action. Strong ideas and storytelling matter more than expensive equipment.
rewards: Selected films could be screened before panel discussions or between breaks.
Depending on quality and partner arrangements, a production house could select a film for further development. No production partner has been named in the guidelines.

criteria.title: Research, interviews, statistics and factual data

notes: AI-generated submission content receives a 15-point deduction, as confirmed on 6 October 2026. AI research or reference is permitted; sources must be credited.

competitions.title: Spoken Word / Monologue
competitions.description: Give your ideas a voice in a two-minute performance rooted in what matters to you.

topics.title: A Day Without Throwing Anything Away
topics.prompt: What would your neighbourhood look like if nobody threw anything away for a whole day? Describe the sights, sounds and small inconveniences to reveal how waste shapes our world.

references.title: National Geographic Kids: Reduce plastic use

topics.title: Redesign an Everyday Object So It Never Becomes Waste
topics.prompt: Choose something you use every day. Explain how its materials, shape or afterlife could change and what that redesign says about the future you want.

topics.title: The Forest Inside the City
topics.prompt: Imagine a forest growing in a busy city. Use vivid imagery or real urban rewilding examples to explore how nature and human life might coexist.

topics.title: Story of Packaging
topics.prompt: Trace a package from convenience and consumption to disposal. Speak as a package, consumer or observer and explore the tension between what packaging promises and what it costs.

topics.title: The Climate Speech
topics.prompt: Share your own hopes, questions, fears or frustrations about the planet’s future and your role in it. Speak honestly rather than repeating familiar statistics.

references.title: Force of Nature: Supporting students with eco-anxiety

topics.title: Data Has a Price
topics.prompt: Speak as someone discovering the climate cost of searches, scrolls and clicks. Make the environmental footprint of digital habits visible.

references.title: Yale Environment 360: AI energy and water
Carbon Literacy: The carbon cost of an email

topics.title: India’s First Green President
topics.prompt: Imagine becoming India’s first Green President. Explain your first policies and the trade-offs you would face, grounded in real issues.

references.title: Right to a clean and healthy environment

topics.title: The Earth — 2080
topics.prompt: Speak as someone living in 2080, in a world shaped by today’s decisions. Paint a vivid future and trace it back to the choices being made now.

notes: Maximum two minutes including the introduction. Submit landscape MP4, up to 50 MB and 1080p, with mandatory closed captions.
Start with: “Hello, I’m [student name] from [school name with city]. The topic for my video is [topic name].”
An additional transcript PDF up to 1 MB is optional; it does not replace the captioned video.
Build an engaging, clearly structured piece, draw on personal experience and offer a fresh insight or call to action.
rewards: Winning entries have an opportunity to be featured on BIG FM or another prime radio channel.
Selected performances could also appear on partner YouTube channels, subject to arrangements.

notes: AI-generated submission content receives a 15-point deduction, as confirmed on 6 October 2026. AI research or reference is permitted; sources must be credited.

competitions.title: Painting
competitions.description: Use colour, composition and imagination to show the potential hidden in what we discard.

topics.title: Waste Segregation: The Future Is Still in Our Hands
topics.prompt: Show how the daily choice to separate materials creates a chain reaction that can reshape our world and put tomorrow within our creative control.

topics.title: Beauty in the Bin
topics.prompt: Challenge the idea that objects lose value when discarded. Discover unexpected patterns, hidden beauty or untold stories in the overlooked and broken, and express the feeling of transformation.

notes: Submit your own original artwork, not a copy.
Include a short sentence or tagline explaining your message.
Use a landscape JPEG or JPG file, up to 1080p and 1 MB.
Create the painting on an A4 or A3 sheet. Use durable, sustainable materials where possible.
rewards: Top three or selected entries are intended for showcase at the Kiran Nadar Museum of Art; summit display depends on feasibility.
Selected artwork may be amplified through prospective partner channels and featured on the Youth Eco Summit website. These opportunities depend on selection and partner arrangements.

competitions.title: Digital Art
competitions.description: Turn an environmental question into an original digital image with a clear message.

topics.title: Beyond the Celebrations
topics.prompt: Explore the environmental footprint of our celebrations. Interpret the tension between collective joy and ecological impact through an atmospheric piece, an eco-tradition or an abstract visual metaphor.

topics.title: The Planet Sent Me an Invoice
topics.prompt: Visualise a bill for every resource you have wasted and your response. Explore ecological debt and responsibility through surrealism, portraits, symbolic landscapes or futuristic design, beyond a literal receipt.

notes: Submit your own original artwork, not a copy.

competitions.title: Waste to Art
competitions.description: Repurpose discarded electronic components into an original model with purpose and imagination.

topics.title: Waste to Art: Crafting Wonders from Waste
topics.prompt: Transform discarded electronics into a creative model. Possible starting points include Green Robot Warriors, Digital Earth, Eco-Bots Rise and The Sorting Station. Explain its purpose, materials, inspiration and environmental impact.

topics.title: Waste to Art: Crafting Wonders from Waste
topics.prompt: Transform discarded electronics into a creative model. Possible starting points include Green Robot Warriors, Digital Earth, Eco-Bots Rise and The Sorting Station. Explain its purpose, materials, inspiration and environmental impact.

topics.title: Waste to Art: Crafting Wonders from Waste
topics.prompt: Transform discarded electronics into a creative model. Possible starting points include Green Robot Warriors, Digital Earth, Eco-Bots Rise and The Sorting Station. Explain its purpose, materials, inspiration and environmental impact.

topics.title: Waste to Art: Crafting Wonders from Waste
topics.prompt: Transform discarded electronics into a creative model. Possible starting points include Green Robot Warriors, Digital Earth, Eco-Bots Rise and The Sorting Station. Explain its purpose, materials, inspiration and environmental impact.

notes: Choose your class band: 5–6, 7–8, 9–10 or 11–12. The common craft prompt applies to all four bands.
Use at least 50% e-waste. The remainder may be other waste materials. A wider variety of e-waste materials can earn bonus consideration; the PDF does not assign bonus marks.
Create the project safely under teacher supervision. Keep construction durable and avoid potential hazards.
Upload two landscape MP4 videos: a 360-degree view up to 30 seconds and an explanation up to one minute. Each is limited to 25 MB, up to 1080p; the two videos together must not exceed 50 MB.
Closed captions are mandatory. An optional transcript PDF can be up to 1 MB.
The student should be visible in the explanation, describing the topic, model idea, materials and inspiration.
rewards: Selected work is intended for Kiran Nadar Museum of Art exhibitions.
Innovative pieces could be displayed in malls or at the summit, depending on durability, transport and venue feasibility.

competitions.title: Eco-Business Model
competitions.description: Pitch an original sustainability business idea with a plan, a purpose and a clear social impact.

topics.title: Green Innovations: Innovating for a Sustainable Tomorrow
topics.prompt: Propose a genuine environmental sustainability business. Waste segregation, e-waste recovery and circular-economy solutions are encouraged, but not required. Define the problem, business model and USP, innovation and action plan, funding needs, and social and environmental impact.

notes: Submit both a presentation PDF up to 2 MB and a one-minute explanation MP4 up to 50 MB.
Use the headings in the organiser’s shared slide template. The template will be added when the team provides it.
Waste segregation and circular solutions are encouraged; any genuine environmental-sustainability business idea is welcome.
rewards: Selected pitches may be presented to corporate and institutional partners.
Standout ideas could receive mentorship or incubation opportunities, subject to selection and partner arrangements.

notes: AI-generated submission content receives a 15-point deduction, as confirmed on 6 October 2026. AI research or reference is permitted; sources must be credited.
